text:
Maria L.: quick q — how are we planning to account for partial tokens on streaming when a client disconnects and then reconnects/resumes? currently looks like we immediately bill token usage as they arrive which can double-count on resume :thinking:
Jake R.: yeah i've seen this twice in prod. client resumes and we replay some tokens. billing ends up counting prefix twice if the resume request generates overlapping tokens
Ola S.: behavior summary from last week: we have per-stream token counter (ephemeral), and a background job that reconciles finalized tokens to the org counter. but the ephemeral state TTL is short (30s) so if reconnect > ttl we commit and the resume will generate duplicates
Kevin T.: proposals: 1) extend ephemeral TTL for resume window 2) provisional-deductions that are reversible until ACK 3) idempotent resume tokens where generator replies are canonical
Maria L.: i like 2) + 1) together. keep short TTL but treat tokens during stream as provisional (not counted against long-term quotas) for e.g. 2m. if client reconnects within 2m we reconcile and only commit the net new tokens. if not, we commit the provisional ones to billing
Jake R.: practical notes: provisioning provisional deductions means we need a separate metric and console UI: streaming.provisional_tokens, streaming.provisional_expiries, streaming.resume_reconciliations. ops needs to be able to see provisional debt per-org
Maria L.: yeah and UX: in console quotas view show a small "Pending streaming usage" row that doesn't count against hard limit until expiry. can add hover explaining resume window
Ola S.: re: fairness — edge case: malicious clients could open many streams and hold provisional tokens to stall billing. mitigations: cap provisional per-key/ per-org and require auth TTL or a small upfront committed token when stream opens (like 1 token deposit)
Kevin T.: that deposit idea is neat. config draft:
```
streaming_rate_limiter:
  mode: provisional
  provisional_ttl_seconds: 120
  provisional_cap_per_org: 5000    # tokens
  provisional_cap_per_key: 2000
  open_stream_deposit_tokens: 5
  max_streams_per_org: 100
  reconcile_job_interval_seconds: 30
  reconnect_grace_seconds: 10
```
Maria L.: also need to decide whether reconnect uses resume token provided by client or we allow a replay window where server tries to dedupe by comparing last_ack_id from client with server-side ack log
Jake R.: recommend server-side ack log + resume token. client sends last_client_ack_id, server finds overlap and trims. that avoids trusting client timestamping. ack log retention should match provisional_ttl
Ola S.: telemetry: emit events when provisional tokens are expired and committed so billing can audit. name them streaming.provisional_committed and streaming.provisional_cancelled
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: rate-limiter/provisional branch -> non-prod at 2026-05-04T02:00Z :white_check_mark:
Kevin T.: one more: how to surface in alerts? we should create alert if provisional_cap_per_org is hit frequently (>=5x/day) or if average provisional expiry ratio > 0.2 (i.e., 20% of provisional tokens expire vs reconcile)
Maria L.: action items: 1) Jake to add metrics + console placeholders 2) Ola to prototype ephemeral ack-log + reconcile job 3) Kevin to draft rate-limiter config & gating rules 4) I'll write a short design note and include cost/billing implications
Jake R.: pulling it into sprint board now. will add a quick spike to measure median resume interval from logs (to size provisional_ttl)
Ola S.: quick snippet for ack-log schema i sketched:
```
ack_log:
  stream_id: uuid
  entries:
    - ack_id: string
      token_count: int
      timestamp: iso
  retention_seconds: 120
```
Kevin T.: cool. if we go with deposit tokens we'll have to update client SDK to include deposit and resume semantics. add to SDK backlog
Maria L.: great thread. let's aim for a non-prod rollout with telemetry only first. follow-ups in #eng-platform. thanks :thumbsup:
